title: Migrate security-lens to contract v2
goal: Update plugins/agent/security-lens to emit a conformant v2 result (result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason) on every exit path, declare router budgets and events in the manifest, fix rc∈{0,1}, add cleanup hook, and cover all paths with tests written first.

steps.description: Write failing tests first (TDD). Extend the existing test file to assert: (a) findings.json carries result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason at top level with plugin data under .data; (b) every verdict the plugin can emit (pass, error) is exercised by a dedicated test case; (c) the no-state_file path returns rc=1 and writes a v2 result; (d) the router-fatal path writes a v2 result with verdict=error and disposition=broken; (e) the cleanup hook exists and returns 0; (f) a golden diff assertion pins the passing-run output shape. Run the suite and confirm each new assertion fails before proceeding.

Update manifest.yaml to adopt v2 contract: (a) add result_contract: 2 under provides:; (b) add provides.events: listing security_lens.failed and any other events the plugin emits; (c) add config.router: block with timeout_s and max_turns (router budgets in manifest, template override still wins per #1816); (d) change valid_verdicts from [] to [pass, error] — the two verdicts the plugin can emit. The existing primary: true on the findings output and the name-matched scope_manifest input (no path/from/type) are already correct.

Update plugin.sh to fully implement v2 contract: (a) add a _security_lens_write_result helper (mirrors _scv_write in spec-coverage) that writes {result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason, data:{}} to findings.json atomically; (b) rewrite the jq -n findings.json output to use this helper — result_contract/verdict/disposition/reason at top level, all current fields (plugin_id, generated_at, findings, stub) move under .data; (c) change both return 2 calls to write a v2 result and return 1 (ADR-054 §4: rc∈{0,1}); (d) the router-fatal path already writes a summary — add a v2 result write before the return 1; (e) add security_lens_cleanup() { return 0; } with an ADR-056 comment (no resources to release; absence is recorded, not implied). The existing stage_summary_write and emit_event calls on every path are preserved.

Run npm test (full bash suite) and confirm green. The spec-acceptance test for manifest valid_verdicts, the security-lens unit tests, and the parity/golden tests must all pass. If any test outside security-lens breaks, investigate before declaring done.

notes: primary:true output: already declared on findings output — no change needed, confirmed in manifest.yaml:61. valid_verdicts: currently [], must change to [pass, error]; review-lens also uses [] because it is advisory and never emits a v2 verdict, but security-lens IS migrating to v2 and will emit verdict=pass on normal paths and verdict=error on router-fatal. cleanup hook: the manifest comment at line 192 ('# ─── cleanup') is a section header, not a function — the function body must be added. rc=2 at plugin.sh:59 (no state_file, security_lens_run) and :90 (missing args, _security_lens_run_inner) — both become rc=1 after writing v2 result. Hard artifact paths: the acceptance criterion says 'no artifact paths in code — assert by grep'; security_lens_run constructs '$artifacts_dir/security${platform_infix}-findings.json' — the platform_infix fanout is a special compound-quality case that may need a note in the test rather than removal, since the manifest output path is fixed as '${artifact_dir}/security-findings.json'. The test's 'platform partitioning' case at line 299 exercises this path; if the grep assertion catches it, the fanout path needs re-examination. Assumption: router budget defaults (timeout_s, max_turns) should match the design plugin (600s, 45 turns) since security-lens is a similar LLM-agent stage. The template override (simple.yaml configures the compound_quality group containing security-lens) still wins per #1816. Golden diff: the spec says 'before/after golden diff on the stage's own output'; no security-lens golden file exists today, so the test must seed it with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 in the green state and then assert it on subsequent runs — standard assert_golden pattern from scripts/lib/golden.sh:8.
